title: Lessons in Chemistry
author: Bonnie Garmus
summary: In the early 1960s, a brilliant chemist is pushed out of the laboratory world and ends up hosting a television cooking show. She treats cooking as science and her audience as capable adults.
readIf: you want a warm, funny story about stubborn competence, sexism and a very good dog.
skipIf: you want a subtle book; the villains are plain and the message is delivered loudly.

pairings.reason: Another cosy, bittersweet novel with a deeply odd animal sidekick and a lonely, capable heroine.
Shares the polite wit and the sense of people building a life with dignity in difficult conditions.
Another story of women pushing against narrow expectations in a mid-century setting, and finding each other.
